evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs, sensitization and challenge with 1-HP, challenge 25 days after last injection
evidence.support_text: Table 4 shows that in the not pre-fed group of 16 guinea pigs sensitized and challenged with 1-HP, 4 animals had a +++ reaction, 5 had ++, 4 had +, and 3 had no reaction. This demonstrates that 1-HP induces delayed-type cutaneous hypersensitivity in guinea pigs, indicating skin sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: repeated dermal contact in guinea pig
evidence.support_text: MNG was evaluated for its ability to elicit a delayed-hypersensitivity response by repeated contact with the skin. MNG produced a response in one guinea pig indicating the possibility of the compound being a weak sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1st challenge on day 21 after initial sensitizing injection; challenge injection route and dose not specified in the provided text.
evidence.support_text: In the experiment summarized in Table 2, after the first challenge (day 21) in 30 guinea pigs sensitized to 1-hydrazinophthalazine (1-HP), 10 animals exhibited delayed-type hypersensitivity (grades + to ++) while 20 showed no reaction (grade 0). This indicates a positive but weak initial sensitization response.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2nd challenge on day 29 after initial sensitizing injection; challenge injection route and dose not specified in the provided text.
evidence.support_text: After the second challenge (day 29) in the same 30 guinea pigs, Table 2 shows 18 animals with delayed-type hypersensitivity reactions (grades + to ++) and 12 without reaction. The intensity and frequency of sensitivity increased compared to the first challenge.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 3rd challenge on day 47 after initial sensitizing injection; challenge injection route and dose not specified in the provided text.
evidence.support_text: After the third challenge (day 47) in 35 guinea pigs, Table 2 shows all animals exhibited delayed-type hypersensitivity reactions, with 1 at grade +, 14 at grade ++, and 20 at grade +++. No animal was grade 0. This demonstrates strong sensitization to 1-hydrazinophthalazine.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4th challenge (day not explicitly given in provided text but presumably after day 47); challenge injection route and dose not specified.
evidence.support_text: After the fourth challenge in 29 guinea pigs, Table 2 shows all animals had delayed-type hypersensitivity reactions, with grades ranging from + to ++++. This indicates further intensification of the hypersensitive state.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5th challenge (day not given); challenge injection route and dose not specified.
evidence.support_text: After the fifth challenge in 29 guinea pigs, Table 2 shows all animals had delayed-type hypersensitivity, mostly at grades +++ and ++++, indicating a very strong sensitization response to 1-hydrazinophthalazine.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 6th challenge (day not given); challenge injection route and dose not specified.
evidence.support_text: After the sixth challenge in 15 guinea pigs, Table 2 shows all animals exhibited the strongest delayed-type hypersensitivity grades: 12 at grade ++++ and 3 at grade +++.
